title: Marketplace onboarding UX scenarios and fallback clauses
body:
Objective:
Purpose: capture end-to-end merchant onboarding flows for cloud marketplace listings (trial/paid), define UX copy variants for edge cases, and enumerate fallback / rollback clauses that operations and legal should accept as defaults. This is a working draft intended to align GTM, Product, and Legal before we hand to Engineering for integration tests.

Background/context:
- We have a handful of partner marketplace pilots scheduled for Q2 2026. These partners expect quick, low-friction onboarding and deterministic failure modes when platform-side gating prevents provisioning (quota, region limits, billing mismatch).
- Primary audiences: marketplace buyers (technical buyers, platform engineers, procurement), partner onboarding engineers, and internal ops runbooks.

High-level acceptance criteria (what "good" looks like):
- Merchant can complete marketplace tile -> trial provisioning flow in <= 5 minutes end-to-end for common clouds (AWS/Azure/GCP).
- When a provisioning failure occurs, user sees clear human-readable action + at least one automatic retry or fallback path without manual escalation in 60s for transient infra failures.
- GTM copy communicates trial limits and data residency clearly; legal fallback clauses are included in onboarding contract snippets.

Key UX scenarios (priority order):
1) First-Time Tile Visit -> Start Trial
   Narrative: user clicks tile, views short benefits + pricing tier, clicks "Start 14-day free trial".
   Success metrics: conversion to trial starts >= 60% in pilot cohort; time to first token < 5 minutes.
   UI copy snippets (short/long):
     - Tile headline (short): "Hosted LLM inference — low latency, predictable pricing"
     - Modal lead (long): "Start a 14-day trial with dedicated vCPU/GPU throughput. No credit card required; switch to reserved capacity when ready."
   Technical gates: marketplace entitlement API returns OK, subscription record created; provisioning job queued with partner-id and region.
   Fallback clause: if provisioning agent fails 3 consecutive times within 2 minutes, present: "Provisioning delayed — we’ll retry automatically. If this persists, contact support@redwood.com with code PROV-RETRY-3." Also enqueue an ops alert (pager) for partner support.

2) Region-unavailable during provisioning
   Narrative: user selects region X; our reserved pools are full or not approved for partner in that region.
   UI copy snippets:
     - Inline warning: "Unavailable in selected region"
     - Suggestion: "We can provision in [nearest region Y] with <5ms median delta. Choose Y or join waitlist."
   Success metrics: 30% of affected users select suggested region; waitlist signups captured and notified weekly.
   Technical gates: capacity-check API returns false; show alternate regions prioritized by latency & compliance.
   Fallback clause: if partner requires exact region and it's unavailable, auto-fail the provisioning but attach a standard clause to partner notification: "Provisioning delayed due to region constraints — expected ETA 7–14 days. Customer billing will not start until provisioning completes."

3) Billing mismatch / marketplace billing not reconciled
   Narrative: billing provider rejects subscription or reconciliation fails.
   UI copy snippets:
     - Modal CTA: "We couldn’t activate your trial because of billing setup. Check your marketplace account or contact billing support"
     - Secondary: "You can still sign up for a self-serve hosted account directly at app.redwood.ai — migration path available."
   Success metrics: >= 40% users offered direct sign-up convert; tickets created for unresolved reconciliations within 48 hours.
   Technical gates: webhook from marketplace returns failure code; surface human-readable reason and marketplace ticket id.
   Fallback clause: allow temporary sandbox (read-only or limited query allowance) for 72 hours while billing is reconciled — with explicit consent and a void-of-liability clause included in the partner notice.

4) Model-variant fallback for capacity throttles
   Narrative: requested high-capacity model variant (e.g., q8_8x) cannot be allocated; we provide smaller-capacity or quantized variant.
   UI copy snippets:
     - Inline notice: "Switched to compatible model variant to preserve latency SLA. Results may vary slightly."
     - Link: "View model differences" (shows per-attribute delta like perplexity/latency)
   Success metrics: application-level errors <1%, average latency meets SLO.
   Technical gates: model routing policy uses variant compatibility registry; logging of variant substitution with telemetry tag.
   Fallback clause: automatic substitution permitted for transient capacity shortages for up to 72 hours. If substitution persists >72 hours, escalate to partner success team and rollback to a paused state pending partner approval.

5) Short-term security audit block (legal/compliance hold)
   Narrative: automated security scan flags partner config or deploy artifact; provisioning should pause while investigation occurs.
   UI copy snippets:
     - Modal headline: "Provisioning paused: compliance check required"
     - Description: "We detected a config that requires a quick review. We’ll hold provisioning until cleared. Expected review time: up to 48 hours."
   Success metrics: median hold resolution <24 hours; partner receives clear remediation steps.
   Technical gates: scan result ID included, link to remediation guide.
   Fallback clause: allow limited sandbox access (no external IO) for troubleshooting; full access blocked until clearance. Legal: partner must accept temporary remediation TOU addendum before sandbox access.

Operational checklist for each onboarding flow (to include in integration tests):
- Verify marketplace webhook signature and mapping to partner id.
- Confirm entitlement -> subscription mapping in Redwood tenant DB.
- Confirm provisioning job created with region, model profile, billing plan.
- Validate automatic retry: 3 attempts at 20s intervals for transient infra errors.
- Verify telemetry tags for any fallback chosen (variant_sub, region_suggested, billing_sandbox).
- Send standard outbound notification templates (partner success + merchant).

Sample outbound notifications (templates)
- Provisioning delay (ops alert to partner and merchant):
  Subject: [Redwood] Marketplace provisioning delayed — action required
  Body: "We attempted to provision your trial but hit a transient error (code: PROV-RETRY-3). We will retry automatically for the next 10 minutes. If provisioning does not succeed, please contact support@redwood.com with your marketplace order id. No billing will occur until provisioning completes."

- Substitution notification (model fallback):
  Subject: [Redwood] Model variant substitution during provisioning
  Body: "To keep your experience within latency targets we temporarily substituted requested model with a compatible variant. This may alter quality slightly. If you require the original variant, reply to this message and we’ll escalate capacity allocation."

Legal + SLA language snippets (to include as optional addenda)
- Trial billing hold clause (short): "Customer billing for marketplace trials will only begin once provisioning is confirmed. Redwood will not invoice for unprovisioned capacity."
- Fallback substitution acceptance (short): "Customer agrees that Redwood may substitute compatible model variants when the requested variant is unavailable; Redwood will notify Customer and provide reversal options where feasible."
- Region-residency ETA clause: "Where provisioning is delayed due to regional capacity or regulatory gating, Redwood will provide an estimated availability window and will not bill until service is available in the requested region."

Open questions / decisions needed (for Legal / Ops):
- Default maximum time for automatic model substitution before escalation (proposed: 72 hours).
- Acceptable trial sandbox scope when billing reconciliation fails (proposed: 2500 tokens/day, no external connectors).
- If partner requires exact-region hard requirement, do we expose a paid "expedite" option to reserve capacity? Pricing + legal needed.

Testing notes for Engineering (integration smoke tests):
- Test harness should simulate: successful provision, transient infra failures, persistent capacity shortage, billing-hook failure, region-unavailable, and security-scan-hold.
- Each simulation must assert: correct UI text surfaced, correct telemetry tag, correct notification template triggered, correct legal clause attached to partner record.

Decision log (recent):
- 2026-02-12: Agreed to automatic retry policy (3 retries @20s) for transient provisioning errors (owners: Ops + Eng).
- 2026-02-20: Legal approved short-form substitution clause; longer SLA addendum deferred.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- GTM: finalize listing short/long blurb and three hero screenshots by 2026-03-24 (owner: Jordan Lee).
- Product: finalize region priority heuristic and fallback UI copy by 2026-03-18 (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- Legal: approve sandbox scope and trial-block language by 2026-03-22 (owner: Amelia Park).
- Engineering: build integration test harness and run pilot in staging (owner: Ravi Menon) — target 2026-04-01.

Notes / references / quick links:

- Related Jira: JIRA-RT-4321 (marketplace webhook retries), JIRA-RT-4365 (model-variant-routing)
